metadata.title: Fantasy Survival Crafting: Every Feature, Played
metadata.audience: makers following the channel's Claude + Walker game workflows
metadata.note: godot-waikthrough walker film. Every gameplay beat is an exact-frame window of a scripted-input take of the real game; no human playtest. Game audio was not captured; narration only. No paid calls, no upload.

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. Hand Walker a design document, and this is the kind of prompt it expects. This one is reconstructed, not a transcript. What came back is a playable Godot game, and this film plays every feature of it, with a script at the controls.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a first-person survival-crafting game — wake in an abandoned valley, gather sticks, gold and stone, craft an axe and a campfire, and survive one night until dawn — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: Built: a 260 m valley, 23 scripts, one night to survive.
Played here: 3 scripted-input takes, 74 of 74 assertions passing.

beats.narration_text: Fantasy Survival Crafting is a race against the clock. You gather and craft through one afternoon in an abandoned valley, light a fire before dark, and survive until dawn. Everything you'll see was played by a script, not a person.

props.text:
Fantasy Survival Crafting
is a crafting game.
Gather, craft, light a fire,
and survive one night.

beats.narration_text: It opens on a sunrise sky: New Game, How to Play and Quit, and no Load Game yet, because there's no save. How to Play lists the controls and seven survival rules.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. Everything the game asks of a player was played and seen working, through real input: gather, craft, chop, hunt, drink, cook, eat, save, load, survive to dawn, and freeze to death. One display defect is on screen: ticked objectives that read zero of three. Whether one night is tense or tedious is a person's call. Nobody has played it yet.

artifactLines: Seen working: gather, craft, chop, hunt, drink, cook, eat, save, load, dawn and defeat.
Defect: ticked objectives read 0/3 once a recipe uses the materials.
Shown honestly: a fire in the water is refused.
Not judged: fun, tension, tuning. 0 human playtests.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude in your own Godot project: Use Walker on my Godot game. Write an input-only capture script that plays one feature through real key and mouse events, asserts what should happen on screen, and fails loudly if it doesn't. Then tell me one thing the capture can't prove. That last part matters: a script that wins is not a player who had fun. Liam, in for Bear.
